content: I'll visually inspect all 11 listed PNGs, starting with the two SI references and two font previews.

All 11 images rendered. Now let me inspect the font previews at full fidelity (region crops around labels/titles) to compare Aptos vs Segoe UI glyphs, and zoom into figure2 and figure3 for glyph/molecule detail.
The first crops mostly caught whitespace. Let me re-crop the label areas precisely and the G4 molecule in figure3.

All 11 PNGs rendered successfully, including native-resolution crops of both font previews, the parity grid, and the G4 structure. Here is the review.

**Font preference: Aptos.** Comparing the two `figureS26_prediction_route_violins.png` previews (identical data/layout), both are clean humanist sans at these sizes and either is acceptable, but Aptos has slightly tighter advance widths and crisper lining numerals ("8/6/4", subscript "2" in log₂), which measurably reduces collision risk in the densest panels (`figure2_QAC105_parity.png`'s 12-panel grid, `figureS28_decoder_error_violins.png`'s 30 violins). Segoe UI is more open/airy — fine if you prefer that calm look, but labels run wider. Subscripts render correctly in both. No missing glyphs in either preview.

**sources/image1.png (historical reference).** Bars + ±1 SD whiskers, value labels above bars, thin grid, readable. Note: the one-line footnote "Error bars show ±1 std…" is a statistical note inside the image; per your style it belongs in the caption. Otherwise consistent; keep as preserved reference.

**sources/image4.png (historical reference).** Layout fine, but each panel footnote shows a visible .notdef box: "□ higher = better" / "□ lower = better". The arrow glyph was not in the rendering font. Fix by removing the arrow or using a supported character; better, move "higher/lower = better" into the caption.

**figure1_supervision_and_transfer.png.** Soft pastel boxes, thin arrows, short labels; good. Colour semantics differ between panels (a: task colours; b: stage colours) but arrows disambiguate, so acceptable. No changes required.

**figure2_QAC105_parity.png.** Marker/glyph system is consistent (lavender circle = Human, mint square = Continuous MIC, orange triangle = Binary MIC, matching `figure5_weight_rewind.png`). Diagonal parity line and a–l panel tags are clean. Points are horizontally jittered by measured value; vertical stacking at discrete measured values is inherent to the data, not a flaw. At journal size the pale lavender points on white are the weakest contrast element — consider a slightly deeper fill or thin darker edge. Row/column headers and shared axes are economical; nothing essential is lost.

**figure3_OOD_families_ACS1996.png.** ACS-1996 depictions are crisp at native resolution; counterions (Br⁻, Cl⁻) legible, including the four stacked Cl⁻ for G4. Subscripts in "CF₃" correct. Layout is airy. Acceptable as-is; if placed at single-column width, G4 (tetra-QAC) will be small but still serviceable for an SI.

**figure4_paired_error_violins.png.** Consistent lavender/mint encoding with figure5; median+IQR glyphs readable; long KDE tails to ~7 are expected. Panel b (OOD17) overlays jittered raw points on the violins — mostly fine, though a few dots sit on top of the median bars; consider a small horizontal dodge or lighter alpha. **Naming inconsistency:** panels read "QAC105" and "OOD17" while figure1 uses "QAC-105" and "OOD-17". Standardise (recommend "QAC-105", "OOD-17" everywhere, including this filename's title strings). Also define "Sa/Ec" abbreviations in the caption.

**figure5_weight_rewind.png.** Correct Δ glyph in "Rewind − intact ΔRMSE"; dashed zero line; marker/colour legend matches figure2. Main issue: in the OOD-17 panel the 95% whiskers reach ~0.58 against a 0.6 y-limit, so caps nearly touch the panel top. Add headroom (e.g., ±0.65) or clip with a caption note. Rotated x labels are readable, no collisions. Per your spec, the "unadjusted 95% paired" explanation is properly left for the caption.

**figureS28_decoder_error_violins.png.** Palette is consistent (grey RDKit, blue Raw, lavender Human, mint Continuous, orange Binary); rotated x labels legible; subscript log₂ correct; median/IQR glyphs clear; tails to ~8 unremarkable. Good as-is.

**figureS29_direct_adaptation.png.** Shared y-axis across the three regimes is the right call (it honestly shows OOD inflation). Points sit in small jittered clusters with short mean ticks; fine. Two nits: (1) the colour-to-method mapping (grey/blue/orange/lavender/mint for Linear/MLP/LoRA/Partial/Full) reuses lavender/mint/orange that elsewhere mean Human/Continuous/Binary — since colour is redundant with the x labels, consider a single neutral colour to avoid cross-figure misreading; (2) there is no legend or caption note explaining the per-category mean ticks — one caption sentence suffices.

**Cross-figure consistency (main actionable list).**
1. Standardise names: "QAC-105" and "OOD-17" (fix `figure4_paired_error_violins.png` titles; align `figure2_QAC105_parity.png`/`figure4` filename stems if convenient).
2. Move statistical footnotes out of `sources/image1.png` and repair the tofu boxes in `sources/image4.png`.
3. Give `figure5_weight_rewind.png` OOD-17 y-headroom.
4. Slightly deepen point fill/edge in `figure2_QAC105_parity.png` for small-size contrast.
5. Optionally de-colour `figureS29_direct_adaptation.png`.

Overall the set meets the stated aim: soft, calm graphics, ordinary readable fonts (Aptos recommended), pastel lavender/mint, thin light grids, short labels, and statistics kept out of the panels. Nothing in these figures implies causality beyond the descriptive statistics you describe.
